answer: A stake-weighted reputation registry makes each agent identity costly to fake: to join the economy an agent must lock a deposit that is slashed if peers catch it running mirror copies of the same persona. Like a prism splitting one beam into verifiable facets, the registry cross-checks work history, payment trails and peer attestations, so a Sybil farm spread across a cold tundra of throwaway accounts still converges on the same stake and the same fingerprints, and spinning up a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits instead of one.
